title: Vision Steering x Text Refusal: Does Image-Side Concept Steering Bypass Language-Side Safety?

original_idea.body: Steering a concept via image-encoder activations on a small open VLM may route around text-side refusal, compounding the multimodal safety gap.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Concrete multimodal jailbreak threat; chain from image-side steering routing around text refusal is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: VLM cross-modal activation steering is more involved (multimodal pipelines, less standard tooling); intermediate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable but cross-modal extraction + text-vs-vision comparison has moving parts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Multimodal steering safety is nearly unstudied, explicit open problem; open VLMs, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Small open VLM inference fits one GPU but multimodal models are heavier.

novelty.reasoning: Image-side concept steering bypassing text refusal appears largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multimodal concept steering as a refusal-bypass is an explicit open problem with little direct published work known.
